heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL IN 4 DAYS (JUNE 9, JSC) — FINAL SRB SEGMENTS EN ROUTE TO KSC BY RAIL; BLUE ORIGIN CEO TARGETS NEW GLENN RTF BEFORE YEAR-END 2026; CREW DAY 56
heroSubtitle: June 5: The Artemis III crew announcement is 4 days away (June 9, 11 a.m. EDT, Johnson Space Center, NASA+/YouTube), when the four astronauts assigned to the redesignated Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test mission (targeting late 2027) will be publicly named for the first time. On the hardware front, the final 8 Artemis III SLS five-segment solid rocket booster segments departed Northrop Grumman's Utah railyard facility on June 2 via Union Pacific rail and are expected to arrive at Kennedy Space Center within the next 2–3 days for summer stacking alongside the SLS core stage (in the VAB since April 28). Marshall Space Flight Center continues fabricating the Artemis III structural spacer barrel and rings. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp announced June 3 that the company is targeting return-to-flight for New Glenn before year-end 2026 using an 'alternative vertical conops' — bypassing full reconstruction of the destroyed transporter-erector. A critical finding from the May 29 LC-36 explosion assessment: the entire propellant farm (liquid oxygen, liquid hydrogen, and liquefied natural gas storage tanks) and the water tower survived intact, removing long-lead infrastructure replacement from the critical path. Blue Origin's only operational pad remains offline; no revised Moon Base I delivery date has been issued. The FAA's mishap investigation into Starship IFT-12's Booster 19 boostback burn failure (May 22) is ongoing — IFT-13 cannot receive a flight license until SpaceX's corrective-action report is approved, with return-to-flight projected no earlier than July–August 2026. The orbital propellant transfer demonstration (mandatory Artemis III HLS qualification milestone) has slipped from June 2026 to Q3-Q4 2026 at the earliest. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 56 post-splashdown at Johnson Space Center, continuing physiological reconditioning. The Artemis II Orion capsule continues de-servicing at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; the heat shield is scheduled for shipment to Marshall this summer for X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions. House Appropriations markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA — flat with FY2026, rejecting the White House's 23% cut. Artemis Accords: 67 signatories (Paraguay 67th, May 7). CLPS 2.0 RFP responses due June 30.
